result.title: ResVision: Spectrum-Matched Resizing and Context-Preserving Inspection for Visual Reasoning
result.summary: Agentic visual reasoning improves vision-language models by selectively enlarging evidence without adding new scene content, but the benefit depends on whether fine structure remains accessible and whether local observations stay grounded in the full scene. We identify three recurring bottlenecks: high-frequency detail can be attenuated during visual-token formation; spatially distributed evidence can remain encoded yet difficult for the language model to retrieve; and isolated crops can weaken whole-detail correspondence through scale and positional mismatch. ResVision addresses these limitations with two complementary components. Spectrum-Matched Resizing (SMR) estimates image complexity and selects an adaptive global sampling scale, avoiding unnecessary enlargement on simple inputs while allocating more visual tokens to detail-rich images. Context-Preserving Inspection (CPI) returns each inspected crop together with the complete working view, preserving local detail and global context across tool turns. We evaluate Direct and Agentic variants on four frontier VLMs and 29 benchmarks spanning six visual-reasoning families. Complete ResVision (Agentic Base plus SMR plus CPI) is best for every model, improving by 3.36 to 4.94 points over Direct Base and 1.87 to 2.94 points over Agentic Base. These results show that adaptive visual sampling and context-preserving inspection address distinct, complementary constraints in multimodal reasoning.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文面向 agentic 视觉推理中的证据放大，指出高频细节在视觉 token 形成时衰减、空间分散证据难以被语言模型取回、孤立裁剪破坏全局对应三个瓶颈，提出按图像复杂度自适应选择全局采样尺度的 Spectrum-Matched Resizing 与每次返回局部裁剪加完整工作视图的 Context-Preserving Inspection，并在 4 个前沿 VLM、29 个基准上评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应 LOOK 环节的收益与成本：以裁剪式证据获取改善视觉细节保留，同时用全局视图缓解尺度与位置错配，可供核查视觉证据筛选、细节信息保真与工具轮次成本之间的权衡；但方法止于输入采样与上下文组织，未涉及 latent 状态生成。
